description: next/ v4 — WMS stock levels (Quant) aligned to SMProfile-Quant (next/). Provides, over the it-edge/BUSINESS path, a business.* stream (entity_type=quant), keyed on the UPSTREAM column 'quant_id' (response.idProperty is an upstream RESPONSE FIELD name, not the smAttribute 'quant_no' it maps to — 2.0.0 named the smAttribute there, so every one of the 500 rows resolved to a null primary key and the source emitted nothing at all; see ci/lint-source-keys.mjs). article_ref + blocked ('gesperrt' column) + quantity ('menge' column) drive the cross-domain deviation material_unavailable: an active OperationsResponse needs article_ref X, sum(free WMS stock X | blocked==0) == 0 -> multi_source discrepancy. Polling was full_refresh up to v2.0.2 (one page per poll, no timestamp diff); v2.1.0 reclassifies it as a timestamp delta - see the 2026-08-30 entry at the end of this description. CAPT-RETRACT 2026-08-18 - VERDICT: THIS SOURCE CANNOT AND MUST NOT BE MADE TO RETRACT BY PAGINATION, and polling.paginate is deliberately NOT set. It IS live (in osf-it-edge-wms SOURCE_IDS) and it-edge (DATA-7) refuses its delete/tombstone pass every 60 s with reason unpaginated_full_refresh - 28 refusals in a measured 30-minute window. THE REFUSAL IS SAVING US. Measured from the refusal lines themselves: seenCount 500, trackedCount 229,054 and RISING (229,120 one minute later), wouldHaveRetracted 228,554. erp.stock_quants holds 3,674,874 rows, ALL distinct quant_id, spanning 2026-07-17 to now and growing 56,011-87,831 rows/day. The endpoint default page is 500 rows ordered by updated_at DESC, so what it-edge sees per poll is an EIGHT-MINUTE SLIVER of a 32-day ledger: the 500 rows returned spanned 16:32:10Z to 16:40:05Z, and two calls 3 s apart shared only 486 of 500. 3,674,491 rows lie OUTSIDE that window and STILL EXIST upstream - so every one of the 228,554 rows it-edge wanted to retract is a LIVE row, and declaring paginate on the assumption that absence means deletion would have been a mass deletion, not a repair. WHY PAGINATION IS THE WRONG MECHANISM HERE, on three independent counts. (1) UNAFFORDABLE: at the server measured hard cap of 5000 rows per request that is 735 requests per poll, every 60 s, at a measured 346 bytes/row = about 1.27 GB per poll = about 21 MB/s sustained against an already overloaded .154. (2) INCONSISTENT: the table grows about 1.3 rows/s, so the population changes while you page it and a page-through can never be a consistent snapshot. (3) UNNECESSARY, and this is the decisive one - THE UPSTREAM NEVER DELETES A QUANT. Consumption sets qty_on_hand to 0 and KEEPS the row: 242,163 zero-qty rows are present, the oldest from 2026-07-17T17:26:41Z. There is no upstream deletion for a retraction to propagate, so cannot-retract is not a defect of this source - it is the correct behaviour, and DATA-7 failing closed is doing exactly its job. THE ACTUAL DEFECT SITS UPSTREAM OF RETRACTION AND IT IS WORSE: this descriptor models an append-only 3.67M-row event LEDGER as a full_refresh stock SNAPSHOT with batchSize 1000. quant_id is not a stable stock identity - it embeds a mint timestamp and its producer (e.g. Q-press-02-20260818163317-_V4_BG-FL-002) - so every production event mints a NEW key. The consequence is measurable in the graph: 378,430 :Quant nodes in the KG, which is neither the upstream population (3,674,874) nor the current stock, but an arbitrary accumulation of eight-minute slivers. PROPOSAL, deliberately NOT applied here because a source already in SOURCE_IDS must not be re-modelled by a descriptor edit alone: either (a) give the WMS a bounded CURRENT-STOCK projection to poll - aggregate to (lager_nr, lagerplatz_id, artikel_nr, charge_nr) with qty > 0, which is the entity SMProfile-Quant actually describes and is small enough to page completely - or (b) reclassify this feed as what it is, an append-only event stream on a timestamp delta (changeDetection timestamp plus timestampQueryParam), which never claims a full population and therefore never asks DATA-7 for a retraction it cannot license. Until one of those is decided, the honest state of this source is INGEST-ONLY, and the 60-second DATA-7 refusal is the correct outcome rather than a bug to silence. DECIDED AND APPLIED 2026-08-30 (v2.1.0, CAPT-WMS) - proposal (b), changeDetection 'timestamp' + timestampField 'aktualisiert_am' + timestampQueryParam 'since'. WHY, and it is not the delta fetch: on 2026-08-25T14:08:47Z this source STOPPED ENTIRELY and delivered nothing for five days. it-edge refused to start its poll loop every 60 s with 'CAPT-KV: eager restore REFUSED - the state does not fit', expected 746,753 / ceiling 600,000 (DEFAULT_MAX_EAGER_ROWS, it-edge state.ts) - a measured OOM boundary inside the 512 MiB container, not a tunable. The ceiling was reached because quant_id is NOT a stable stock identity: it embeds a mint timestamp and its producer, so every production event mints a NEW KV key over an UNBOUNDED key space, measured at +52,617 keys/day. Raising the ceiling is therefore not a fix but a date: 1,000,000 buys about 4.8 days. changeDetection 'timestamp' is the fix because it changes the RESTORE PATH, not the fetch: PollEngine.start computes deferred = (changeDetection === 'timestamp' && !needsWholeSet), and a deferred restore calls store.loadDeferred(), which materialises ZERO rows (loaded: 0, rows: {}) and never consults the ceiling at all - rows are looked up per key via getRow(). needsWholeSet is false here because SMProfile-Quant declares only 'on_change' and 'never' promotion tokens and has no parentType, so minIntervalMs() is null and no periodic re-emit walks state.rows. This is exactly the class erp-bde-confirmations (KV 1,010,721, ABOVE the ceiling and a measured heap-OOM on the eager path) and sim-v5-qms-inspections already run in, for weeks. KV population is thereby irrelevant to this source's restore FOREVER, which is why (b) is permanent and a higher ceiling is not. MEASURED LIMITATION, recorded so nobody reads more into this descriptor than is true: the upstream IGNORES the timestamp parameter. Probed 2026-08-30 against the live source .154:38224 - GET /api/wms/quants?limit=5000&since=<2027 future> returns 5000 rows and &since=<2020 past> returns the same 5000; every candidate spelling (since, updated_since, modified_since, changed_since, aktualisiert_seit, from, after, ts_since, since_ts, *_gte, start*, min_updated_at) and every format (ISO-8601 with and without ms, date-only, epoch s, epoch ms) behaves identically, while limit= demonstrably works and an invented parameter changes nothing - i.e. unknown parameters are silently dropped. The exemplar sim-v5-qms-inspections carries timestampQueryParam 'since' and its upstream .154:38261 ignores it in exactly the same way (500 rows for future, past and no parameter alike), so this is the family's behaviour and not a regression here. The parameter is declared anyway because it is inert today (silently dropped) and becomes correct the moment sim-v5 implements it; it is NOT load-bearing for the fix. CONSEQUENCE, and it is not a loss: each poll returns the newest page ordered by aktualisiert_am DESC (server default 500, hard cap 5000 - verified strictly descending across a 5000-row page spanning 2026-08-30T05:00:39Z to 15:08:11Z, i.e. about 8.2 changed rows/min), so a 60 s poll of 500 rows carries roughly 60x the observed per-window churn and about 13x the churn implied by +52,617/day. RETRACTION IS UNCHANGED AND STILL REFUSED: polling.paginate REMAINS UNSET, and the single-shot REST fetch now returns the DATA-7 verdict 'timestamp_delta' instead of 'unpaginated_full_refresh' - both are incompleteFetch, so this source may ingest and may still never retract. CAPT-RETRACT's verdict above therefore stands unweakened: the 228,554 rows it-edge once wanted to retract are live rows, the upstream never deletes a quant, and pagination here would be a mass deletion. Proposal (a), the bounded CURRENT-STOCK projection, remains the right MODELLING fix and is explicitly still open - (b) revives the lane and removes the ceiling as a failure mode; it does not turn an append-only event ledger into the stock snapshot SMProfile-Quant describes.
